Hi Ava / Ethan —

Thanks again for the call this morning — really appreciate the context on Acme's priorities for document understanding and extracting structured data from claims. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (from our discovery)
- Primary use case: ingest claims PDFs and extract claimant info, policy IDs, and line-item amounts for downstream workflows.
- Volume: ~20k docs/month, spikes up to ~80k in quarter-end.
- Success criteria: 95% precision on key fields, <200ms 95th percentile latency on single-document extraction, and clear cost per 1k docs estimate.
- Compliance: data residency in US, SOC2 evidence required.

Proposed next steps
1) Evaluation kickoff (30–45m): align on trial plan, success criteria, sample prompt set / evals, and access requirements
2) Demo & technical deep dive (45–60m): Neha to walk through ingestion pipeline, model selection (open models + quantization options), and integration points
3) Trial execution: Redwood provides a 2-week sandbox with an eval harness and sample prompts; Acme shares a small prompt set + representative sample documents

Suggested times for the kickoff (all PT):
- Tue 2026-03-23 10:00–10:45
- Wed 2026-03-24 13:00–13:45

I'm attaching a short evaluation plan and a proposed demo agenda for your team to review. Can you confirm which time works (or share alternate availability)? Also would be helpful if you can send: 
- a short list of stakeholders who should join the kickoff (names + roles)
- a sample set of 15–30 documents (anonymized) or a pointer to where we can pull them from
- any hard constraints for success metrics we should include in the trial plan

Looking forward to the next steps.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | (415) 555-0134
